title: Same Average? Mean Deviation Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Two classes write the same test and both have an average of 50 marks. In one class everyone scored close to 50; in the other, marks run from 10 to 90. How do we put that difference into one number? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 13, Statistics) we learn the mean deviation.

You will watch both classes on one number line while each mark's gap from the average is drawn live and added up: a total of 6 for one class, 120 for the other, so mean deviations of 1.2 and 24. Step by step we see why the signed deviations always cancel to zero, why we take absolute values, and reach M.D. about the mean and about the median. A side-by-side of the mean and the median with one far value, a pause-and-think question, the NCERT worked example (answer 2.75), the exam trap of forgetting the bars, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:

2:37 Worked example (NCERT): answer 2.75

3:34 Where it is asked
3:46 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:28 Recap and three questions to answer
